decisions.thought: Bring Garchomp lead for rocks/eq, Gholdengo (blocks status, sweeps with NP), Kingambit as late cleaner. Skip Primarina/Rotom/Dragapult—opponent has Kingambit and Gholdengo that resist them. Watch for their Incineroar Intimidate and Dragapult speed.

Opp team: garchomp, dragapult, kingambit, gholdengo, primarina, rotomwash. My bring: Incineroar lead (Intimidate, Fake Out, Parting Shot), Garchomp (Mega), Gholdengo (Scarf). Plan: Incineroar pivots into Garchomp or Gholdengo. Watch for Primarina and Rotom-Wash.

Garchomp lead vs Incineroar. EQ likely OHKOs/2HKOs; Incineroar may switch to Corviknight or Gholdengo. Set rocks early while I'm fast. Intimidate cut my Atk—EQ still strong. Keep Kingambit for late, Gholdengo blocks status. Watch for their Dragapult speed.
Turn 1: Fake Out on their Garchomp to stop its first move. Next turn, Parting Shot into Gholdengo or my Garchomp. Their Garchomp is already at -1 Atk. Watch for Rough Skin recoil on contact moves.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Against the opposing Garchomp, Fake Out gives priority chip and a flinch while costing some HP to Rough Skin if that's the ability, which seems acceptable. I'm weighing Fake Out followed by Parting Shot next turn versus switching, since Parting Shot itself is too slow to beat Garchomp's speed this turn and stacking two Atk drops would leave Garchomp at -2.

After that I'd pivot Gholdengo in on the scarf set, though I'm second-guessing the matchup since Ground moves hit Steel hard and Shadow Ball isn't great damage against Garchomp. Still, Fake Out is the right call to open with.

decisions.thought: Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar; EQ likely OHKOs (87% HP, SE). If they switch, EQ hits switch-in or I can set rocks later. Take the KO now—Fake Out is spent. Keep Kingambit/Gholdengo fresh; expect Corviknight or Gholdengo switch-in (immune to EQ), then pivot to Gholdengo.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
So after the Trick, Gholdengo now holds Leftovers while Garchomp ends up with the Choice Scarf — meaning Garchomp will be locked into whatever move it picks next, since the scarf lock only kicks in once they select a fresh move with it equipped.

I'd also mistakenly flagged Gholdengo as immune to Earthquake, but Steel/Ghost just takes neutral damage, not immunity — that Earthquake at -2 Atk still dealt roughly 98 damage, dropping Gholdengo to 64 HP, so another hit would knock it out. With Garchomp now scarf-boosted, speed order is murky, but I need to assume they'll outspeed and threaten lethal damage next turn.

Switching my own Garchomp in looks safest, since it'd only take minor Earthquake chip at -2 Atk while absorbing the hit, letting me mega evolve and counterattack afterward. Attacking with Gholdengo risks death if they outspeed, since even Make It Rain wouldn't KO Garchomp outright, so I'll go with the Garchomp switch.
